## 1. The precise organizing principle

Fix a known source channel
\[
\Gamma:M_a\longrightarrow M_b.
\]

Define \(p_k^*(\Gamma)\) as the supremum of all probabilities \(p\) for which there exist:

1. A channel \(E\) with exactly \(\Gamma\)’s specified complete all-reference RLD/maximal-information profile.
2. A CPTP \(k\)-receiver channel whose marginals all equal \(E\).
3. A receiver-local, trace-nonincreasing CP operation satisfying
   \[
   \mathcal R_{\mathrm{succ}}\circ E=p\,\Gamma.
   \]

This last equality is a channel identity. Its success probability is independent of the unknown input, including when that input is entangled with an untouched reference. The optimization allows arbitrary finite local output dimension.

The resulting trichotomy is:

| Source class | Optimal heralded recovery |
|---|---|
| Entanglement breaking | \(p_k^*(\Gamma)=1\) for every \(k\) |
| Non-entanglement-breaking, saturation YES | \(p_k^*(\Gamma)=\Theta_\Gamma(1/k)\) |
| Saturation NO | Some finite order \(K\), and every \(k\ge K\), admits no such same-profile broadcast |

For the middle case, the bounds are explicitly
\[
\boxed{
\frac{c_\Gamma}{k}
\le p_k^*(\Gamma)
\le
\min\!\left\{
1,\frac{\log_2 a}{k\,E_{\mathrm{sq}}(J_\Gamma/a)}
\right\}.
}
\]

Here \(E_{\mathrm{sq}}(J_\Gamma/a)\) is the squashed entanglement of the **normalized Choi state**. It is positive for every non-entanglement-breaking source, including sources with PPT-entangled Choi states. The constants depend on the source. This proves the optimal exponent; it does not assert the generally unsupported bound \(p\le 1/k\) with unit constant. The converse uses established monogamy, strong monotonicity, and faithfulness results for squashed entanglement. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

The condition

says that no nonzero degree-one class disappears upon localization at \(\ell\).

The useful lemma is:

The corresponding residue field is a finite extension of \(K\), so the resulting quotient is finite-dimensional over \(K\). Repeating on the remaining kernel separates the whole finite-dimensional space.
